Connect your PRD, GitHub activity, and refresh snapshots into one project state board.

About.feature3Desc: Capture how the original thesis and current direction changed, with the reason and evidence attached.
About.testimonialsTitle: Understand the project you built with AI

About.proofTitle: A state board, not another pile of notes
About.proofDesc: You should not have to dig through AI chats, commits, PRs, and scattered docs just to remember where the project stands.
About.proof1Desc: See what is done, at risk, blocked, or still open against the current PRD or working plan.

About.introContent: Hello. Synapso is a project memory tool for people building products with AI. Code piles up fast, but the reason behind each decision and the current project state disappear just as quickly. We are here to reduce the time it takes to recover that context.
About.backgroundQuote: Why do AI-built projects lose context after just a few days?
About.backgroundContent: Synapso.dev restarted from this question. AI makes implementation faster, but decisions get scattered across chats, commits, PRs, and notes. We are building <important>a workflow that connects PRDs and GitHub activity to continuously recover the current project state</important>.
About.nameContent: The name Synapso comes from the feeling of a <important>synapse</important>, the connection point where signals become something the system can use. Projects have the same kind of connection points. PRDs, commits, pull requests, issues, and AI conversations are scattered signals on their own. When connected, they become usable memory. Synapso.dev is the place that stores those signals as project memory.
About.diff1Desc:
Synapso stores project state as snapshots against the current plan, not as loose commit summaries.
That makes the project comparable over time.
About.diff2Desc:
AI judgments are backed by commits, PRs, issues, and the plan document.
You should be able to inspect what the model saw.
About.diff3Desc: When the original goal and current direction diverge, Synapso turns product, scope, and execution changes into explicit drift items.
About.diff4Desc: We do not use your code for AI training. We follow strict security principles where data is discarded immediately after analysis, valuing your code assets.
About.visionQuote: AI-built projects should not lose their context
About.visionContent: Synapso.dev is not trying to make more text. It is trying to become the project memory that helps you make the next decision faster.

HowItWorks.title:
Connect scattered work signals
into project memory.
HowItWorks.step1Desc: Start with one real project. Record the name, description, original thesis, and current thesis so the board has a baseline.
HowItWorks.step2Title: Attach a PRD or working plan
HowItWorks.step2Desc: It does not need to be perfect. Add what you are building, what done means, and what remains so AI has a basis for state tracking.
HowItWorks.step2PlanPlaceholder: Example: v1 goal, key user flow, this week's hypothesis, open work items...
HowItWorks.step3Desc: Pick a repo from your signed-in GitHub account. Recent commits, PRs, and issues become evidence during refresh.
HowItWorks.step4Desc: AI reads the plan and GitHub activity together, then stores a snapshot. Like a synapse connecting signals, progress, phase, risks, blockers, and watch-next items become one project memory.
HowItWorks.step5Desc: Plan changes become drift items, and run history shows what input the model used instead of forcing you to guess. When you come back later, you can follow the project's memory again.

prdTemplate.title: Use this structure to write the current plan
prdTemplate.description: Synapso uses this document to judge progress, blockers, risks, and drift. It does not need to be a polished PRD, but the objective and acceptance criteria should be concrete.
prdTemplate.copyHint: Move only the useful parts into the input

checklist.objective: The problem this project solves and the v1 goal
checklist.users: Who will use it and in what situation
checklist.scope: What is in scope and out of scope for this pass
checklist.acceptance: How you will know the work is done

prdTemplate.markdown:
# PRD

## 1. Background
- Why this project is needed.
- What problem exists today.

## 2. Objective
- The main goal for v1.
- What should change for the user if this succeeds.

## 3. Target Users
- Primary users.
- The situation where they would use this feature.

## 4. Core Scenario
1. Where does the user start.
2. What input or choice does the user make.
3. What result should the user see.

## 5. Scope
### In scope
- Features that must be included in this version.

### Out of scope
- Work that will not be handled in this version.

## 6. Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The user action that must succeed.
- [ ] The result the system must save or display.
- [ ] The change that should appear on the Synapso state board after refresh.

## 7. Risks and Open Questions
- Decisions that are not settled yet.
- Technical uncertainty.
- Assumptions that need user validation.

## 8. Current Progress
- Completed work.
- Work in progress.
- Next work to do.

review.title: Review this snapshot
review.summary: Does the summary describe real work?
review.summaryReady: The current summary reflects actual work instead of baseline filler.
review.summaryMissing: If the summary still feels generic, the prompt needs tighter guidance.
review.watchNextReady: The current watch-next items read like real follow-up work.
review.watchNextMissing: If watch-next is short or vague, it should be pushed toward executable next actions.
review.evidence: Does the evidence connect to real changes?
review.evidenceReady: At least one of commits, PRs, or issues is attached as real evidence.
review.evidenceMissing: If evidence is empty, the GitHub context is still too thin.
review.planCoverageReady: The board captured at least two plan-progress items.
review.planCoverageMissing: If plan coverage is too thin, the PRD likely needs clearer structure.

hints.summary: Start by checking whether `Current snapshot` explains the key decisions behind the code changes.
hints.watchNext: Check whether `Watch next` is something you would actually do in the next session.
hints.evidence: Compare `Commit coverage`, `PR evidence`, and `Issue evidence` with the real work context.
hints.secondRefresh: After a bit more work, run a second refresh and check whether the deltas still make sense.

secondRefresh.title: Second refresh validation
secondRefresh.empty: Do a bit more work, then run `Refresh state` again. From the second snapshot onward, this board can validate deltas and drift sensitivity.
secondRefresh.progressMissing: If progress stayed flat, check whether the new work actually made it into the snapshot.
secondRefresh.driftStable: Drift stayed flat. If the direction did not really change, this is reasonable.
secondRefresh.driftChanged: Drift changed by {value}. Check whether that matches actual product-direction changes.

hints.workMore: Do a bit more work before triggering the second refresh.
hints.checkDelta: Compare `Change since last snapshot` with what actually changed in the project.
hints.checkDrift: If tiny implementation changes create large drift jumps, the detector is too sensitive.
hints.runs: If something looks off, inspect the latest snapshot source and raw output from `View runs`.
